claims.text: The initial catalyst is a near-equiatomic multi-principal-element automotive alloy catalyst.
The initial catalyst has baseline catalytic activity.
The initial catalyst has moderate poisoning resistance.
The initial catalyst has limited lifetime durability under real-exhaust aging.

A closed-loop protocol integrating automated solvothermal synthesis, accelerated aging, activity screening, machine learning, and Bayesian optimization can identify an improved, slightly adjusted near-equiatomic composition.
The intervention iteratively adjusts catalyst elemental ratios.
Composition optimization will produce optimized local atomic arrangements and modified active-site distributions.
The optimized structure may contain tailored Cu–Ni domains enriched or doped with minor amounts of platinum-group-metal substitutes.
The modified active-site distribution will promote efficient oxidation.
The modified local structure will resist sintering and poisoning.
Fine-tuning interactions among catalytic sites will reduce oxidation activation energies at low temperatures.
Composition optimization will enhance stability against poison-induced deactivation and thermal-cycling degradation.
The optimized catalyst will improve oxidation activity below 150 °C by more than 20% relative to the baseline.
The optimized catalyst will have greater resistance to H2O and NO poisoning than the baseline.
The optimized catalyst will have greater durability under accelerated aging than the baseline.
The predicted improvements apply to simulated transient, low-temperature exhaust containing H2O and NO and to accelerated thermal and chemical aging.
The effect may not extend to extreme pollutant concentrations or substantially different operating temperatures.
The proposed experiment compares optimized variants with the initial near-equiatomic catalyst under low-temperature exhaust, poisoning, and accelerated-aging tests.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant activity improvement of at least 20% together with superior poisoning resistance and durability would falsify the hypothesis.
